topic: Centralizing Spring MVC validation errors with ProblemDetail
tomorrowTopic: Choosing stable API error codes versus human-readable messages

hook.headline: Validation errors are part of your API contract
hook.hook: A centralized handler can turn Spring MVC binding failures into one predictable Problem Details shape without leaking controller-specific exception handling everywhere.
hook.visualCaption: Spring validation failure → advice → ProblemDetail → client

mentalModel.title: Separate detection from representation
mentalModel.coreIdea: Bean Validation detects invalid request values; Spring MVC raises a web exception such as MethodArgumentNotValidException for invalid @Valid request bodies. A controller advice can translate that failure into a stable ProblemDetail representation for clients.
mentalModel.keyOutcome: Controllers stay focused on successful use cases while validation failures share one documented HTTP error contract.
mentalModel.mentalShortcut: validation decides what failed; advice decides how the API says it

code.title: Map binding failures once
code.intro: A REST advice can convert request-body validation failures into RFC 9457 Problem Details plus a deliberate extension field.
code.highlightReason: ProblemDetail supports non-standard properties, letting the API add structured field errors while retaining the standard problem fields.
code.takeaway: Centralize transport-level error representation, and expose only fields and messages you intentionally make part of the API contract.
code.professionalNote: Spring MVC supports ProblemDetail and ErrorResponse directly. ResponseEntityExceptionHandler is also a framework-provided base for handling built-in MVC exceptions when you want broader centralized customization.

production.title: Keep the error contract stable
production.scenario: Several React forms call different endpoints and currently receive inconsistent validation payloads, forcing endpoint-specific client parsing.
problems: Per-controller handlers drift into different JSON shapes.
Raw exception details or unstable framework messages can accidentally become client dependencies.
Field names can expose internal DTO structure if transport models are not treated as API contracts.
production.professionalApproach: Define a documented Problem Details shape, centralize MVC validation translation, add structured extension fields deliberately, and test status, media type, error codes/fields, and representative invalid requests.
production.debugClue: If a validation failure bypasses this handler, identify which MVC exception was actually raised; method-level validation can follow a different exception path from request-body argument validation.

interview.question: Why centralize Spring MVC validation errors with ProblemDetail instead of handling them in every controller?
interview.answer: Centralization separates validation detection from HTTP representation. Spring MVC can detect and expose validation failures, while a controller advice produces one documented Problem Details contract. That reduces duplication, keeps controllers focused on application behavior, and prevents clients from depending on arbitrary exception text. You still need to handle the actual exception paths your endpoints use, including method-level validation where applicable.
remember: Bean Validation detects invalid input; it does not define your public error contract
ProblemDetail provides standard fields and supports deliberate extension properties
Different MVC validation paths can raise different exceptions, so test the endpoint behavior you expose
